content: LLM grounding and hallucination in multi-section narrative reports: Five failure modes that pass schema validation but are substantively wrong: (1) Enum hallucination — picks valid enum values that are semantically wrong; (2) Confident fabrication — free-text fields return plausible invented data even when schema constrains structure; (3) Cross-field contradiction — individual fields pass but contradict each other; (4) Distributional collapse — LLM generates generic safe values across all inputs; (5) Array hallucination — fabricates array entries rather than returning empty arrays. For multi-section reports vs. single blocks: risk compounds across sections because each independent prompt/section has its own hallucination surface; numbers mentioned in prose interpretation sections are NOT covered by schema constraints on the recommendations array. Schema validation alone is insufficient — a post-generation runtime guard that cross-checks cited values against computed diagnostics is necessary. GSAR framework: partitions claims into grounded/ungrounded/contradicted/complementary with evidence-typed scoring.
